rationale.a: Code minimum kitchens at 63 SF cannot accommodate standard appliance configurations, counter workspace, and proper work triangle; standard practice requires 10 ft × 12 ft (120 SF) minimum for functional residential kitchens.
rationale.b: While compact living is common in condominiums, 63 SF at code minimum sacrifices functionality; the professional concern is delivering inadequate living space, not density accommodation.
rationale.c: PD 1096 minimums apply to residential uses generally, not exclusively single-family dwellings; the concern is about adequacy, not legal applicability.
rationale.d: A separate pantry does not compensate for inadequate kitchen area; the kitchen itself must be functional for daily food preparation regardless of auxiliary spaces.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 specifies minimum kitchen area of 5.4 m² (approx. 58-63 SF) for residential units. However, code minimum produces cramped, non-functional spaces. Standard practice allocates 10 ft × 12 ft (120 SF) minimum for kitchens accommodating refrigerator, stove, sink, counter space on multiple walls, and circulation. The distinction between code-compliant minimum and professional design standard is a critical ALE concept.
